article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Bubblegum × Burmese
Breeder: Vancouver Island Seed Company
THC Content: 19-23% range
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Bubblegum, sweet fruit, citrus, floral spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-autumn
Indoor Yield: About 90–115 grams per plant
Outdoor Yield: Variable
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Long before candy-flavored marijuana became one of the dominant trends in modern breeding, Dubble Bubble was already combining unmistakable sweetness with energetic old-school cannabis genetics. The Vancouver Island Seed Company cultivar joins Bubblegum with Burmese, producing a hybrid that can smell like pink chewing gum one moment and sweet citrus, flowers, herbs, and spice the next. Its appeal is not based on extreme THC numbers or exaggerated visual traits. Instead, the strain belongs to an earlier school of breeding in which recognizable flavor, sturdy plant structure, and a balanced experience carried as much weight as laboratory potency.

The name requires some clarification because several unrelated cannabis strains called Dubble Bubble or Double Bubble now circulate. The version covered here is Vancouver Island Seed Company’s historical Bubblegum × Burmese hybrid. Contemporary seed sellers also market a Dubble Bubble descended from Bubblegum and OG Kush , while other breeders have used similar names for Bubblegum backcrosses. Those cultivars should be treated separately. Historical VISC records consistently connect its Dubble Bubble with Bubblegum and Burmese.
Genetics and Lineage

Bubblegum provides the familiar sweet side of the pedigree. Classic Bubblegum genetics became famous for flowers capable of producing an unusually convincing sugary chewing-gum aroma accompanied by berry, floral, and earthy undertones. The parent also contributes dense calyx development and a somewhat broader flower structure. Vancouver Island Seed Company’s own description of the cross emphasized Bubblegum’s tendency to add weight through clusters of thick calyxes and long pistils.

Burmese changes the architecture and character considerably. The Burmese line used by Vancouver Island Seed Company was sativa-oriented, contributing stronger branching, a more open plant frame, and a brighter aromatic component. Combining it with Bubblegum created a plant that retained identifiable characteristics from both parents rather than simply tasting like a sweeter version of one side. Period strain records specifically noted that Burmese branching remained visible in Dubble Bubble even as Bubblegum increased flower density.

The pairing also helps explain the hybrid’s balanced personality. Bubblegum contributes sweetness and relaxing body qualities, while Burmese brings more cerebral energy and a somewhat lighter growth pattern. This makes the cultivar substantially different from modern Bubblegum × Kush interpretations sold under the same name.
Effects and Experience

The experience generally begins above the shoulders. Moderate consumption can bring a noticeable improvement in mood, mental brightness, and increased interest in conversation, music, or casual activities. Rather than producing an immediate rush or intensely stimulating high, the effects tend to develop in a smoother progression. That character fits the genetics well: Burmese influence keeps the early phase lively, while Bubblegum prevents the experience from becoming overly sharp.

Physical relaxation appears gradually. The body may feel looser without becoming immediately heavy, making moderate amounts potentially suitable for an afternoon or relaxed social setting. Increased intake shifts the balance toward a calmer, hazier experience, and some consumers may eventually prefer sitting rather than remaining active.

Because surviving breeder material predates today’s standardized cannabis testing industry, fixed THC claims should be viewed skeptically. Later descriptions often place the strain around the upper teens or low 20% THC range, but the actual strength of preserved or recreated material can differ substantially. Consumers should rely on the laboratory certificate for the specific flower in front of them rather than assuming that every Dubble Bubble shares identical potency.
Medical Benefits

Dubble Bubble has not been studied as an individual medical marijuana cultivar in controlled clinical trials. Any therapeutic reputation therefore comes from consumer experience and from broader research involving THC-dominant cannabis rather than research on this particular strain.

Its combination of mood elevation and later physical relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers seeking temporary help with stress, poor appetite, minor discomfort, or difficulty unwinding. The less abrupt onset may also be attractive to people who prefer marijuana that does not immediately create a heavy couch-lock sensation.

As with other THC-rich weed, higher doses can produce unwanted effects including dry mouth, dizziness, impaired concentration, increased heart rate, or anxiety. Medical consumers should judge the actual cannabinoid content of their specific product and speak with a qualified healthcare professional when cannabis may interact with medications or existing health conditions.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The Bubblegum ancestry is obvious, but the aromatic profile extends well beyond candy. Fresh flowers can produce sweet chewing gum, ripe fruit, citrus peel, flowers, and lightly earthy herbs. Grinding the buds often intensifies the sweeter elements while exposing sharper green and spicy notes inherited from the Burmese side.

On the palate, sugary fruit usually arrives first. The sweetness can resemble classic pink bubblegum rather than the syrup-heavy candy aromas of modern Runtz-style weed. Citrus and floral qualities appear through the middle of the inhale, while a mild earthy or herbal finish keeps the flavor from becoming cloying.

No original laboratory terpene profile has been preserved, so assigning a definitive dominant terpene would be misleading. Aromatic characteristics are compatible with compounds such as limonene, myrcene, caryophyllene, and pinene, but actual concentrations would need to be established through modern testing of a verified genetic sample.
Growing Information

Vancouver Island Seed Company described Dubble Bubble as a plant that visibly retained Burmese branching while developing thicker Bubblegum-influenced flowers. This produces a hybrid structure rather than the squat, tightly stacked form associated with many modern indicas. Branches can spread outward and benefit from training that keeps the canopy even and exposes secondary flowering sites to light.

Historical breeder information places flowering at approximately seven to nine weeks. One particularly useful detail from the original description is the relationship between root volume and production. In a two-gallon container, the breeder reported roughly 90–115 grams, or about three to four ounces, per plant and specifically noted that yield increased in proportion to root mass and overall plant size. This suggests the cultivar responds well when given enough root space rather than being pushed into undersized containers.

Flower structure combines thicker Bubblegum calyx development with more open Burmese-derived branching. Growers should still maintain strong airflow as flowers gain weight, but the plant is not generally described as an extremely compact, moisture-trapping cultivar. Outdoors, adequate sunlight and unrestricted root development can allow the Burmese influence to produce a larger frame than many growers expect from a strain carrying Bubblegum genetics.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Dubble Bubble?

The original Vancouver Island Seed Company version is Bubblegum × Burmese. Historical strain lists associated with the breeder document that combination. Newer cultivars using the same or similar name may have completely different genetics.
Who bred Dubble Bubble?
The version covered here was created by Vancouver Island Seed Company, a Canadian breeder whose catalog included numerous Burmese-based hybrids during the 2000s.
Is Dubble Bubble indica or sativa?

It is best described as a hybrid with meaningful sativa influence from Burmese. Bubblegum adds denser flower structure and relaxing qualities, while Burmese contributes branching and a more uplifting cerebral component.
What does Dubble Bubble taste like?
Expect sweet bubblegum, ripe fruit, citrus, floral notes, mild herbs, and earth. The candy character is noticeable but typically less syrupy than many modern dessert strains .
How long does Dubble Bubble take to flower?

Historical breeder information places flowering at roughly seven to nine weeks indoors. The ideal harvest point can vary with phenotype and environmental conditions, so trichome maturity and overall flower development remain better indicators than calendar days alone.
Final Thoughts on Dubble Bubble

Dubble Bubble offers a useful glimpse into cannabis breeding before extreme THC percentages and dessert genetics became the center of the market. By combining Bubblegum with Burmese, Vancouver Island Seed Company created marijuana that preserved recognizable qualities from two very different parents: dense, sweet Bubblegum flowers and the branching, brighter character of a Burmese sativa line.

Its history is particularly important today because the name has been reused. Garden of Green and other breeders have released different Dubble Bubble or Double Bubble cultivars, sometimes involving OG Kush or Bubblegum backcrosses. Those may be legitimate strains in their own right, but they are not genetically interchangeable with the Vancouver Island Seed Company original.

For enthusiasts interested in older Canadian genetics, classic Bubblegum flavor, or strains that provide a more balanced experience than today’s ultra-potent hybrids, the original Dubble Bubble remains an interesting reference point. Sweet without being one-dimensional, relaxing without immediately becoming heavy, and structurally influenced by both sides of its pedigree, it represents a style of weed where flavor and breeding character matter just as much as raw potency.
